title: Apple's First Foldable iPhone Reaches Stores; Supply and Durability Are the Next Tests
dek: The iPhone Duo launched Friday at about $2,000 with constrained availability. Apple's design ambitions now face a real-world test of production scale and foldable-screen reliability.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: An iPhone 16e displayed outside an Apple Store; an earlier Apple model, not the newly launched foldable

keyPoints: Apple began selling the iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, on October 23; the company lists a 7.6-inch inner display and an A20 Pro chip.
Reuters described the launch price as about $2,000 and supply as limited; model availability varies by market.
Reports of early screen cracking remain anecdotal; Apple has not established a widespread defect, and the cause and scale are unclear.
body:
Apple's first foldable iPhone went on sale Friday, turning a long-running product bet into a live test of customer demand, supply and device reliability. The iPhone Duo carries an approximately $2,000 starting price, Reuters reported, and the company describes a book-style design with a 7.6-inch inner screen and a 5.4-inch outer display. Apple said the device was available in stores worldwide on October 23, though its model page notes that additional countries and regions would receive availability on October 30.

## The product case

Apple is positioning the device as both a smartphone and a larger multitasking surface, rather than simply another premium phone. Its announcement says the inner display is its largest on an iPhone and highlights fold-specific software, a precision hinge, Apple's A20 Pro processor and a dual-battery design. A foldable form can make video, reading and side-by-side apps more comfortable, but it also introduces a hinge, a flexible display stack and new durability questions that standard slab phones do not face.

Early availability has been constrained. Reuters described limited supply and reported that Apple expected to capture a large share of the foldable category's value despite entering it years after competitors. That forecast came from research firm IDC, not from reported Apple unit sales, and should be read as an estimate. Macworld's October 25 buyer guide said preorder delivery estimates had stretched into late January in the U.S. and that walk-in inventory was limited in selected markets. Such waits can reflect a supply bottleneck, strong initial demand or both; they cannot, alone, establish the eventual sales trajectory.

## Reliability claims require evidence

The launch has also drawn online reports of cracks near the inner screen's fold. Macworld summarized some early owners' complaints and said the cause and scale were unclear. The reports are not a statistically representative sample of devices, and Apple has not announced a broad recall or confirmed a systemic defect. It would be premature either to declare the model defective or to dismiss the complaints. Early failure rates, repair turnaround and warranty response will provide better evidence as more devices are in use.

The financial stakes are meaningful because Apple must deliver a new form factor without compromising the reliability that supports its premium pricing and resale value. A constrained launch can defer revenue if production cannot scale, but it may also help avoid overbuilding inventory before demand is visible. Investors will watch whether the new category attracts buyers beyond early adopters, and whether foldable demand adds to the iPhone franchise rather than cannibalizing higher-priced models.

## What to watch next

The next-country rollout on October 30 should expand the pool of buyers, while Apple's next quarterly results—date not confirmed by the company as of this edition—will offer a first official read on the phone's commercial contribution only if management chooses to discuss it. The company has not broken out iPhone Duo sales separately. Investors should focus on total iPhone performance, availability and customer feedback rather than treating pre-order wait times as equivalent to sell-through.

For consumers considering a foldable, the choice is less abstract now: compare the larger inner screen with price, hand-feel, app support and service terms. For Apple, the challenge is to turn a high-profile launch into a repeatable, scalable product line. Sources: [Apple's September product announcement](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/), [Apple's launch-day store report](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/10/iphone-duo-arrives-at-apple-store-locations-worldwide/), [Reuters on market positioning and supply](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/apple-bets-iphone-duo-can-remake-foldable-market-sales-begin-2026-10-22/), and [Macworld's October 25 availability and issues roundup](https://www.macworld.com/article/2629813/iphone-duo-folding-design-guide-problems-price-specs.html).

marketImpact.summary: The foldable rollout creates a potential new premium-product growth stream for Apple, but constrained supply and unverified durability reports introduce execution risk that matters more than early launch buzz.
marketImpact.timeframe: Next 2-4 weeks; more evidence with Apple's next quarterly update

tickers.rationale: A successful premium launch could broaden iPhone revenue, but limited production, a high price and unresolved reliability reports make near-term execution uncertain.
A new Apple form factor could support premium smartphone component demand if it scales, but Apple's product sales are not yet disclosed and component exposure is indirect.

catalysts.event: Apple says iPhone Duo becomes available in 28 additional countries and regions
Apple's next fiscal-quarter earnings date has not been company-confirmed; treat market calendar estimates cautiously
